nodes.description: During brain development, loss of p130 reduces neuron numbers and causes neural apoptosis in mouse embryos, and Rbf loss in flies reduces brain size. In patients the head is usually of normal size at birth and microcephaly develops postnatally, so the human counterpart of this node may be a failure of postnatal brain growth rather than of embryonic neurogenesis. p130-null mice die in mid-gestation only on some genetic backgrounds, and full nulls in flies and mice are lethal, whereas human patients with truncating variants survive.

nodes.description: p130 with E2F4 and the MuvB core forms the DREAM complex, which binds cell-cycle gene promoters in quiescent cells and represses them. The authors of the largest series propose that such de-repression could disturb neuronal development, excitability or synaptic release; this has not been tested.

nodes.description: Neuronal dysfunction that persists after brain development. In Drosophila, the RBL2 orthologue Rbf is required in differentiated post-mitotic neurons for normal locomotion, and re-expressing it in adult neurons rescues the locomotor defect of Rbf hypomorphs. Rbf mutants also have altered sleep timing and loss of evening anticipation. In cultured rodent neurons, depleting p130 causes neuron death. By analogy, loss of RBL2 in mature human neurons may contribute to the motor and sleep phenotypes and may be partly reversible; there are no human neuronal data.
